title: Welded Asteroids
description: The closed-loop stigmergic field itself, living on the quotient surfaces of the topology game: physarum agents, trail and agent-deposited momentum all obey the surface's gluing rule. Six tour levels bind surface + parameter presets + a beta_1 target; 18 declared sliders drive the physarum; the asteroids game survives as a hidden Easter egg (X when beta_1 >= 42). v2.0.1: seam crossings now transform position AND heading together (topo-asteroids flipP protocol — fixes agents stranding at the Klein/projective seams); sim square letterboxed to true 1:1 (fixes stretched height map). v2.1.0: the real fix for the Klein seam-wall — three compounding defects. (1) foldRead/momRead/uvOf mirrored the WRONG axis (topo.y.flip='x' names the axis that mirrors; the code mirrored the other one), so agent sensing disagreed with deposits. (2) Diffusion sampled neighbors with plain torus wrap; on a mirrored identification the flux at the seam never cancels and mass was slowly pumped into the two seam rows — the minutes-scale accumulator. Now neighbor sampling honors the gluing rule (mirrored cell across a mirrored seam) for trail AND momentum, with the vector's mirrored component sign-flipping. (3) Sense samples crossing a mirrored seam have swapped left/right meaning relative to the agent's square frame; the turn rule now swaps L/R when the front and a flank read different fold images — near-seam agents no longer turn back into the seam. Also fixed: wrapPos wrap-count for negative coordinates (floor division) and double-flip when a y-fold pushed x out of range. Verified: 150s Klein soak — no seam wall, no edge pinning; torus/projective/Mobius 45s soaks all stable. v2.2.0: the height map projects the topology — 3D vertices displace along their base normal by the folded trail height (ridges = built loops, valleys = evaporated field), texture texels fold so the parametrization shows the true pullback at every seam, contour lines and agent points ride the same displaced surface, and a '3D relief' slider (0..1) controls the amplitude. Lit MeshStandardMaterial with key/rim lights so relief reads as form. v2.3.0: color separation + seam-continuous contours. Chemical field stays green; contour overlays recolored to the violet family; agents drawn as cyan-white dots (2D overlay + 3D points) so they read against the chemical; wireframe seam guides dimmed violet. Contour segments touching a canvas edge are redrawn shifted by the wrap so closed loops read continuously across the weld instead of chopping off. v2.3.1: operator-reported 3D misalignment (left planes not lining up) — root cause: the v2.2.0 texture/relief path folded the uv a second time (guessing the parametrization needed the sim's mirror), but the surface parametrization already IS the folded immersion; the extra fold split the texture along a line the geometry never folds. foldUv is now the identity — the gluing lives in the parametrization and the sim-side foldRead, exactly once each. v2.3.2: Codex co-review (gpt-6-astra, read-only) confirmed the operator's residual 3D misalignment was a VERTICAL TEXTURE FLIP — three.js CanvasTexture defaults flipY=true, so texture rows ran opposite to the height sampling rows. Fixed with flipY=false. Two follow-on defects from the same review: entities (contours, agent points) now ride the ACTUAL displaced mesh via barycentric interpolation instead of the analytic surface (they floated/sank between mesh vertices), and relief 0 now restores base positions instead of freezing the last displacement. v2.3.3: hardened the overlay against a devicePixelRatio desync — the canvas is sized and transformed with the DPR live at fit time, but the draw paths re-read devicePixelRatio, and a window dragged to a display of different pixel density changes it without firing resize. Scale is now committed once per fit (ovSX/ovSY), a matchMedia (resolution: Ndppx) listener refits on density change, and a ResizeObserver on the sim panel covers layout changes that never resize the window. NOTE: this was a real latent defect but NOT the cause of the operator's report — see v2.3.4. v2.3.4: the actual cause of the operator-reported quarter-size overlay — drawContours computed the grid→CSS scale and then never applied it. buildContour emits paths in GRID units (0..W) because segStore is reused for the 3D push, so the strokes must carry the scale themselves; without it contours drew one grid unit per CSS pixel, filling a W-sized patch in the top-left of an s-sized box. The error is W/s, so it is invisible when the sim panel is about W wide and grows with the window — which is why it read as 'quarter size' on a wide window and looked fine on a narrow one. Strokes now run under octx.scale(sx,sy) with line widths divided back out so the authored weights hold; segStore stays in grid units for the 3D push. The test port exposes __welded.ovScale so the registration can be measured rather than eyeballed. Verified at a 1355x760 viewport: violet contour centroid (0.711, 0.518) against field centroid (0.716, 0.527) on the sim canvas — agreement to within 0.01 of the canvas, where the pre-fix overlay centroid sat at (0.336, 0.334) against a field centroid of (0.500, 0.498). v2.4.0: the 3D shell is now a declared render mode — translucent (new default), wireframe, or solid. A closed quotient surface occludes its own far side, so the opaque shell hid exactly what the panel exists to show: the loops, contours and agents on the back of the torus, and the figure-8 Klein's pass-through entirely. The lever is depthWrite, not opacity — a transparent shell that still writes depth hides everything behind it however see-through it looks; translucent and wireframe both drop depthWrite so the whole shape reads at once. The mode is reapplied on every surface rebuild and is drivable from the test port via __welded.setShell(), with state().shell reporting it. v2.5.0: the sim became runnable as an experiment rather than only watchable. The physics was inside the rAF callback, so it advanced only while the page was painted — a hidden tab froze it and a run's length was wall-clock, not step count. simStep() is now the unit of time and loop() is one simStep plus one paint. Every stochastic draw goes through a seeded stream (mulberry32), spawn can be 'disc' (the ancestor's, still the interactive default) or 'uniform', and the test port gains pause/resume/step(n) plus run(spec) — {seed, surface, spawn, params, at:{step:{...}}, steps} — which returns a manifest that replays identically. PARAMETERS ARE PINNED TO THE TIMELINE: a change is declared at a step index, fires exactly once there, is recorded in the manifest, and drives the slider so the panel cannot show 60 degrees while the sim runs at 90. A run mutated by hand mid-flight is not reproducible, which is how a reported state became unrecoverable. Verified: identical seed reproduces the grid bit-for-bit, a different seed does not, a scheduled change alters the outcome and still replays, and stepping runs at full CPU with the page hidden. v2.5.1: three code paths disagreed about which axis a mirrored weld flips. topo.<axis>.flip NAMES the mirroring axis — Klein is y:{flip:'x'}, so crossing the y-seam mirrors x. wrapPos (agent re-entry) and diffuseDecay's nbT (trail diffusion) read it that way; foldRead mirrored the CROSSED axis instead, so an agent sensing past the weld read the field from a point its own deposits never reach, and momRead flipped vx — per its own comment, which states the correct rule — while folding the coordinate in y. Verified at (40, H+10) on the Klein: re-entry (260,10) and diffusion (259,10) against sensing (40,289). foldRead now honours the named axis; __welded.ablate({seamFold:'legacy'}) reproduces the old path as a control. MEASURED AND NEGATIVE: this does NOT remove the Klein seam accumulation. Uniform spawn, seeds 11 and 22, 4000 steps, both arms end at 11-12.5x the uniform expectation for the rows either side of the weld, against 0.0-0.3 on the torus control. The inconsistency was real; it is not the cause of the accumulation, which remains unexplained and may be genuine dynamics — a mirror line is a natural condensation locus for a physarum network. v2.6.0: slice scope — a planar section of the torus at height c cuts the surface in two circles; the trail is sampled on both and their per-theta difference is normalized by the clamped dimensional radius rho_c = R + sqrt(max(0, r^2 - c^2)), the section's actual radial reach. The diff profile encodes the plane the physarum structure lives on: flat ~0 means toroidally uniform, +mean is an outer-wall (equator-like) loop, -mean a bore (polar) loop, and a sinusoidal diff is a tilted/Villarceau-like band whose first-Fourier phase reveals the plane's orientation and whose amplitude the off-plane share. Panel: z slider, hi/lo/diff strip chart, live rho_c, Delta-bar/rho_c, amp and phase readouts; also exposed on the test port as __welded.slice(). v2.7.0: quadrant scope + gyroscopic readout — two orthogonal planes through the torus axis carve the ring into four quarter-sections whose trail masses are live (the 'clean quarter slice'). The torus provides the reference frame: the field's center of mass is computed every frame directly from the grid, mapped through the embedding to xyz, and reported in toroidal coordinates — rho (radial offset from the central ring), z, and omega, the per-step precession rate of the COM about the axis (frame-to-frame theta difference). The quadrant panel shows the ring from above with cutting planes, quarter-mass arc thickness, the COM marker displaced by rho, and a 120-step precession trace. Balanced ring = COM on axis, omega ~ 0; a tilted off-axis structure shows a nonzero rho with a precessing theta — the gyroscopic reading. On the test port: __welded.com(), __welded.quadrants(). v2.8.0: collector plates — the four quarter-sections reframed as accelerator pickup electrodes (beam-position monitor): the readout is the normalized difference b = (b_x, b_y) = ((Q_R - Q_L)/(sum), (Q_U - Q_D)/(sum)) in [-1,1]^2, which divides out total trail intensity entirely. |b| is how off-axis the field's mass sits, atan2(b_y, b_x) is the steering angle (the precession angle in BPM dress), and the trace of (b_x, b_y) over time is the precession plot — total-charge-free and comparable across runs. The panel shows the four plates at the rim brightening by collected charge, the steering vector on a crosshair, and a 180-step trace. Balanced beam reads (0,0) at any brightness; a beam hugging one plate reads toward +-1. On the test port: __welded.plates(). v2.9.0: mobile/fold experience — the 3D pane takes touch-action:none so one-finger drag orbits instead of scrolling the page, plus two-pointer pinch zoom (distance delta drives camera distance, pointer capture per pointer, cancel-safe). On narrow or coarse-pointer screens the three fixed panels (sidebar | sim | 3D) become a stacked tabbed stage: a two-tab bar (sim / 3D) switches which pane is full-width, and the control sidebar becomes a slide-in drawer behind a fixed hamburger toggle. Desktop layout untouched (media query only). v2.10.0: Villarceau scope — the third slice family as an instrument. A plane tilted alpha from the equator cuts the torus in a loop pair whose topology flips at the critical angle sin(alpha*) = r/R (26.74 deg on the sim's R=1, r=0.45 embedding): separate pair below, exact tangent (Villarceau, linked circles) at, interlaced pair above. The scope solves the section condition per tube angle (n-hat . torusXYZ(u,v) = d is linear in cos u, sin u -> 0/1/2 roots), samples the trail on both branch curves, and reads per-v traces plus first-harmonic amp/phase and a loop-correlation 'link' scalar that climbs toward 1 as the loops merge (measured: 0 at alpha=0, 0.89 at alpha=85). The obliquity dial is free 0-90 deg with the critical angle and live regime (separate/tangent/interlaced) labeled on the panel — the obliquity of the slicing plane is itself a probe coordinate, completing the multidimensional-oscilloscope chart alongside the equatorial slice scope and the axial quadrant scope. Design doc: docs/villarceau-scope.md. Verified headless: regime classification flips exactly at alpha*, 0 page errors, port __welded.vill()/VLS. v2.10.1: Villarceau scope solver correction + honest readouts (post adversarial review: GPT-6 Astra via Codex, plus an earlier independent review; both instrument records preserved). HIGH: villSection solved the wrong equation — the plane condition A(v)cos u + B(v) = d has B constant in u (z-term), but v2.10.0 treated it as a sin-u coefficient (atan2/acos phase-shift form) and sampled near-misses of the true plane (residual up to ~0.7 tube radii). Correct roots u = ±arccos((d-B)/A); sampled points now satisfy the plane condition to 1e-15. HIGH: alpha=0 degeneracy — the centered section reduces to the equatorial pair; villSample(alpha=0) now delegates to sliceSample(c=0), passing the design doc's agreement test that v2.10.0 failed (mean diff 2 vs 0 on a synthetic field). SEMANTICS: same-plane tangent section circles CROSS TRANSVERSELY (53.49 deg on this torus) — 'tangent' is plane-torus contact, not circle-circle tangency; same-plane sections are coplanar so linking number is 0/undefined; the linked Villarceau pair is same-handed circles from DIFFERENT rotated critical planes (verified Gauss linking -1 at 60 deg azimuth). 'link' readout relabeled 'agree' (uncentered cosine similarity — not Pearson, not linkage; scene-dependent); added 'sep' = minimum 3D separation between branch curves. Dial snaps to alpha* within +-0.5 deg; regime labels separate/near-alpha*/separated; stats computed over valid samples only; plot scale no longer mixes angle column into amplitude; readout split into three short lines that fit the canvas; dead VREC/VLS.trans removed; design doc revised (docs/villarceau-scope.md v2). Core theorem sin(alpha*) = r/R survives both reviews; alpha* = 26.744 deg on the sim torus. v2.11.0: external confinement field + energy ledger (docs/confinement-field.md). Tokamak analog: field lines are exact slopes dv/du=q on the quotient chart — the safety factor as geometry. Three knobs: winding q, coupling kappa, cross-field drift nu; three modes: closed (byte-identical v2.10.1 behavior), field-on (open system, P_in billed), field-decaying (single-run tau_sim shutoff protocol). Energy ledger: P_in = kappa*40/q (injection), P_loss = trail evaporation + drift leakage, W_stored = coherent trail mass + momentum coherence, tau_sim = W/P_in. q-histogram: per-agent winding number peaks at the driving rational under strong coupling — VERIFIED: locks at 2.02 for q=2, coherence 0.99 (rational-surface resonance analog, the prediction from the tokamak mapping thread). Bootstrap window (stigmergic substitution for external confinement) instrumented via kappa-reduction protocol; result pending experiment. v2.11.0-rc bug caught in verification: confDir returned slope q^2 (1/q,q); fixed to (1,q) → q locked correctly. v2.11.1: q-histogram instrument correction. v2.11.0 accumulated HEADING vectors (cos a, sin a) with a decay — agents parked on the field direction have the front/back degeneracy (a and a+pi give the same tan) and the decay drove the winding-number distribution onto a fixed attractor (~1.8) DECOUPLED from the driving q; the rational-lock verification of v2.11.0 was this bug reading as a lock (q-peak read 2.02 at every q). Fixed: accumulate wrap-aware chart-position deltas — the path's TRUE winding number q_agent = dv/du. Verified: q-peak now tracks driving q monotonically (q=1 -> 1.02, 1.5 -> 1.27, 2 -> 1.68, 2.5 -> 2.02, 3 -> 2.48, all at coherence 1.000). Residual ~0.83x under-read at high q is real cross-field displacement (momentum advection + drift), not instrument error — 'effective q vs nominal q' is now a measurable quantity. Also: v2.11.0 sweep finding recorded — P_loss under-bills drift by ~2 orders (parts x nu vs evaporation-dominated loss); tau_sim is drift-insensitive; ledger loss model needs actual cross-field heading error (queued v2.11.2). v2.11.2: no-bugs-stand pass (internal audit + adversarial review, Astra usage-limited mid-run; its finding folded in). CRITICAL: field-decaying mode was dead — P_in multiplied by CF.decay=0 snapped to 0 AND full coupling kept steering (free field); now P_in decays (shutdecay=0.97) and coupling decays with it (effKappa = kappa * sqrt(P_in/P_in0)) — the shutoff protocol actually measures confinement decay. HIGH: confinement field was not globally well-defined on mirrored surfaces (Klein/projective/Mobius): uniform slope-q maps to slope -q under the seam flip — confDir now transforms through flipV per seam image (position-dependent via the fold); q-histogram deltas likewise flip-transformed across mirrored seams. HIGH: W_stored momentum term was raw magnitude (scaled with intensity, mislabeled coherence) — now true alignment fraction in [0,1]. MEDIUM: P_loss under-billed drift ~2 orders (billed the dial value) — now bills actual cross-field heading error mean|sin(field-heading)| per agent. MEDIUM: qAccum/qPrev stale after resetField (ghost deltas) — cleared on reseed. LOW: dead code removed (confApply stub, lastW); field-arrows checkbox now draws a real seam-aware arrow overlay (CF.arrows). Verified: shutoff P_in monotonically decays 18->14.99 over 7s, tau finite through decay, structure retention 1.077 (field decayed, structure held — first bootstrap-flavored signal, pending proper experiment); Klein coherence 0.998 with seam-aware field; 0 page errors. v2.11.3: Opus-review fix pass. Ledger computes in ALL modes (closed-mode early return blinded the shutoff experiment). W_stored = trail CONTRAST (excess mass above uniform mean), not trail mass — the old metric saturated at ~175k for fog and field alike; the cold-closed control matched the field-on steady state exactly, killing the v2.11.2 'bootstrap signature' claim (measurement refutation, not physics). Cross-field error/leak only computed against an ACTIVE field (phantom-field artifact removed: cf read 0.65 in closed mode against a field that wasn't there) and scales with applied coupling in decaying mode. Momentum term = true alignment order parameter |sum mom|/sum|mom| (old mean-magnitude was a density proxy latched at 1). tauSim only defined at constant P_in (field-on); decaying-mode tau must come from structure-decay fits (b1/slice-FWHM), not a vanishing denominator. P_in0 decay reference seeded before first decay step (off-by-one). Drift is a true CROSS-FIELD kick (perpendicular to field lines), not isotropic jitter. VERDICT from the fixed instrumentation: post-shutoff W rise (90k->138k) matches the cold-closed control (92k->145k) at identical saturated coverage — the W/contrast metric cannot distinguish structure from diffusion transient; bootstrap remains UNPROVEN. Discriminating instruments for the next pass (Opus-specified): beta-1 persistence, slice-FWHM, quadrant-omega lock, and a new internal-coherence readout (heading vs trail-momentum, not vs the external field). v2.11.5:  v2.11.5: Pauli-exclusion analog for the agents (occupancy blockade, per the crowding-control precedent from boid_drafting). Two dials: exclR (occupancy radius in cells, 0=off) and exclK (stiffness 0-1: soft = heading-coincidence-weighted steering away from occupied cells via the seam-aware momentum field; >=0.75 hard = veto of the chosen move onto an occupied cell with stochastic second-choice fallback and pin counting). Occupancy is LAGGED (built from previous-frame positions on the BASE image via foldRead — mirror images are the same physical place on the quotient) and order-invariant; gated so exclR=0 is bit-identical to v2.11.4. Pressure readout exclReject (rejections/step) + pin rate in the manifest. Motivation: exclusion adds the fermionic half of the phase diagram (degeneracy pressure; band-filling); connects to twistronics flat-band regime (interaction-dominated when kinetic quenched). MEASURED v2.11.5 (post-review, with controls): exclR=0 bit-identical to v2.11.4 after all fixes (checksum 17500000.02153451). C1 self-repulsion bug found by Claude Code review, fixed (lone-agent step length flat 1.012 across exclK 0-0.7; pre-fix it rose to 1.79). Counters reset per run + dedicated rndExcl stream (arms share physarum noise); foldRead negative-coordinate mirror fixed; occTmp removed; jitter ablation control added (exclMode). Final sweep (seed 77, N=7000, 4000 steps, kappa 0/0.3/0.8, arms: control / excl-soft K=0.5 / jitter / excl-hard K=0.9): (1) kappa=0.8 user regime — control b1 collapses 21->0 by 2500 steps; exclusion and jitter arms both keep b1 alive (2-8) through 4000 steps — structure preservation is REAL but perturbation-strength-mediated, NOT exclusion-specific (jitter control matches). (2) kappa=0.3 — the finding: soft exclusion CRYSTALLIZES the swarm into ~11 parallel slope-1 lines (perpendicular rms 6.4 cells vs 81.8 control; jitter control only narrows to 43.8) — a genuine filled-ladder/1D-crystal state, exclusion-specific, OPPOSITE sign to the widen prediction. The old filled-shell refutation is RETRACTED: at moderate coupling exclusion produces band-filling after all, as parallel copies of the band rather than a wider band. (3) q-lock survives all arms (q 0.95-1.0, coherence 0.94-1.0). Documented caveats: hard mode is a lagged blockade (same-frame double occupancy possible); soft kick up to 1.9 cells/step can overshoot the stencil; heading-coincidence clause is coarse (momentum lattice MS=8 vs stencil R<=3) — soft exclusion acts as density repulsion except at momentum-block boundaries. v2.11.6: version badge (top-left, sim+3D); 3D auto-spin removed — orbit fully drag-controlled.

cogdoc.claim: The closed-loop stigmergic field's native domain is a quotient surface: agent writes and reads both obey the surface's gluing rule (mirrored re-entry on Klein/projective/Mobius, walls on the strip), so the simulation itself provides the levels and the beta_1 readout is measured on the surface the structures actually live on.
